results.evidence: The test is parametrized over all four key parts (url, observed_at, excerpt, observation). Each case imports a record, then re-imports the same record with exactly one evidence field changed (deepcopy, then changed[part] = CHANGES[part]). It asserts the output reads '(+1 evidence)', that evidence rows rise by exactly 1, that the lead count is unchanged, and that the rows are the original item followed by the changed one. This matches cottonwood/prospects.py, where _evidence_key (lines 306-309) is the tuple (url, observed_at, excerpt, observation) and _insert_new_evidence (lines 312-329) inserts only items whose key is not already stored. I ran the file with `uv run --offline pytest -q tests/test_prospects_evidence_dedupe.py` and all 7 tests passed.

The test imports one record with two identical evidence items. It expects 'imported 1, matched 0, rejected 0' and exactly one evidence row. The file's 7 tests pass (7 passed). _insert_new_evidence adds each new key to the `stored` set after inserting (prospects.py:327), so the second identical item is skipped. That matches the one-row result.

The test file passes (7/7). Its _counts reads every non-sqlite_ table from sqlite_master. The test asserts the first import prints 'imported 3, matched 0, rejected 0', then that the second prints f'imported 0, matched {len(rows)}, rejected 0' and that _counts(db_path) == before. I also ran the real CLI on a temp db with a 3-row CSV. The first import printed 'imported 3, matched 0, rejected 0'. The second printed 'imported 0, matched 3, rejected 0' with exit code 0. Row counts for all 7 tables (organizations, contacts, leads, evidence, activities, agent_runs, suppression) were identical before and after: 3/0/3/3/3/0/0.

results.evidence: In the worktree, `uv run --offline pytest` exited 0 with 936 passed. `uv run --offline ruff check .` exited 0 with 'All checks passed!'. `uv run --offline mypy .` exited 0 with 'Success: no issues found in 106 source files'. `uv run ruff format --check .` exited 0 with '316 files already formatted'. The `--offline` form of the format check failed on every try, but the cause is the environment. uv tried to rebuild the local package and could not find `hatchling` in its cache, so ruff never ran. Run directly as `.venv/bin/ruff format --check .`, and as `uv run ruff format --check .` without `--offline`, it passed and reported 316 files already formatted.
